what: Rendered-layout evidence for every live calculator route, at two measured viewports. This is the artifact behind criterion B of `pnpm check:done`: AGENTS.md states that nothing in the test suite checks appearance, so a green suite says nothing about layout, and 'someone looked at it' does not survive a session ending.

method.tool: in-app browser, same-origin iframes at an explicit width against the BUILT export served from out/
method.why: An iframe with width=390 gives the document a real 390px layout viewport, so the page's own media queries apply. Measurements are taken from the iframe's contentDocument after two animation frames.
method.rejectedApproach: chrome --headless --screenshot --window-size=390,844 . On this machine the headless window clamps to a minimum somewhere between 500 and 560 CSS px: captures at 390 and at 500 came back PIXEL-IDENTICAL in their left 390 columns, while 560 and above reflowed. So a 390-wide file from that path is a wider layout CROPPED, not a phone layout. It looks like valid evidence and is not. Any future harness must verify the layout width it claims, not just the image width.
method.verified: Every row's iframe reported contentWindow.innerWidth exactly equal to the requested viewport; that assertion is recorded per viewport below as viewportVerifiedForAll.

findings.noPageLevelOverflow: At 390 and at 1280, no route produced documentElement.scrollWidth greater than the viewport. Where a table is wider than the screen, the horizontal scroll is contained by the ResultTable wrapper, which is the intended behaviour.
findings.ruleVersusSymptom: docs section 3 requires mobileCards from five columns up. Measurement shows column count and rendered overflow are independent: lai-kep has 5 columns and does NOT overflow at 390, while vay-thuong-mai and lai-suat-thuc-te have 4 columns each and DO overflow. The threshold is a proxy for the symptom and is wrong in both directions. The two 4-column rows are deliberately NOT added to WIDE_TABLE_PENDING, because that list is the allowlist for the RULE and is checked both ways — a non-violator listed there would be reported as a stale entry. RE-MEASURED 2026-09-16 AFTER THE FIX: both 4-column rows now report ZERO elements over 390 and are removed from elementsWiderThanViewport above (11 rows -> 9). vay-thuong-mai went 485px -> 300px inside its 300px frame; lai-suat-thuc-te moved to mobileCards, so below md it renders no table at all. NARROW_OVERFLOW_MEASURED is now empty. The finding itself still stands and should NOT be deleted: the column threshold remains a proxy that is wrong in both directions, and lai-kep still has 5 columns without overflowing.
findings.emphasisStableAcrossViewports: The same 30 rows ship at least one <strong> at both viewports, with identical counts, so reading emphasis does not vary with layout.
findings.causeWasHalfWrong: The earlier record said the cause on both 4-column rows was Vietnamese header length. Per-column measurement showed that held only for lai-suat-thuc-te. On vay-thuong-mai the headers merely matched the width of the cells beside them; the binding constraints were an 8.5rem prose label floor misapplied to a column of 1,2,3 (136px for content needing 32px) and untyped money cells, which opted the table out of the compact reading and pinned each amount column at the width of 5.000.000.000 (125px). Shortening its headers alone moved the table 380px -> 380px, i.e. no gain. Widest-text-in-column is not the same as the reason the column is that wide.
findings.loanCompareRoutesFixed: so-sanh-khoan-vay and lai-co-dinh-hay-tha-noi are two routes over one component (LoanCompareCalculator), so one change to costBarsModel cleared the six-column docs-section-3 violation on both. Re-measured at a verified 390px viewport on 2026-09-16: both report ZERO elements over 390 and are removed from elementsWiderThanViewport (9 rows -> 7). The recorded design objection to carding the comparison table did not survive measurement: its rows are OFFERS and its columns are metrics, so a card per row is a per-offer cost summary, and the metric-across-offers view a comparison wants already exists on the same page as the 281px So sanh tung chi tieu table. Fixing that table then exposed a second overflow on the fixed-vs-floating route only: a FOUR-column payment table at 427px, caused by a composed option label held on one line by nowrap. Letting it wrap puts it at exactly 300px on both routes.
findings.noRowOverflows390: As of 2026-09-16 NO live calculator route has an element wider than the 390px viewport. The list went 11 -> 9 -> 7 -> 0 across three changes: the two four-column rows, the two loan-comparison routes, and finally the seven-row P3/P4 shelf (eight tables: diem-pivot, gop-401k, toi-da-401k, ira-truyen-thong-hay-roth, nien-kim, rut-toi-thieu-bat-buoc and both tables on phan-tich-thu-nhap-huu-tri). Removed slugs and their last recorded counts: diem-pivot=9, gop-401k=13, toi-da-401k=31, phan-tich-thu-nhap-huu-tri=25, ira-truyen-thong-hay-roth=13, rut-toi-thieu-bat-buoc=27, nien-kim=10. An EMPTY list here is the goal state, not a broken sweep — the guard in components/calc/wide-table-pending.test.ts had a non-vacuity floor asserting more than five overflowing rows, which would have gone red on completion, and it was removed for the same reason STATUTORY_UNDECLARED and NARROW_OVERFLOW_MEASURED lost theirs.
findings.remainingRuleDebt: WIDE_TABLE_PENDING still holds ONE entry, lai-kep: five columns, so it violates docs section 3, and measured to FIT at 390px. It is a rule debt with no rendered symptom, which is the clearest surviving evidence that column count and rendered overflow are independent.

measuredSeparately.method: Real viewport emulation in the Claude in-app browser against the built export on localhost, with window.innerWidth read at capture time rather than assumed. NOT the iframe method the 2026-09-16 sweep used. AT 390 THE PANE RENDERS 1:1 AND THE OBSERVATIONS BELOW ARE FROM SCREENSHOTS. At 1280 the pane scales the emulation down and screenshot capture returned blank, so the 1280 evidence for this row is DOM-derived only (innerWidth 1280, no page-level overflow, condition cards 628 px) and is not a visual observation. Recorded that way on purpose.
observed: 390, from screenshots: title, lede and the three-condition notice render legibly; the calculator opens at 5,4 / 300 / 80; the LTV help reads “đây là quy định, không phải giả định”; all three condition cards in `SocialHousingConditions` render as readable bg-soft blocks; the five limits render as a bulleted list; the FAQ accordion shows five items; and both decree links render as underlined brand-green-ink (rgb(17,127,54)) anchors with their notes beneath.

A DEFECT WAS FOUND AND FIXED IN THIS PASS: the limits list shipped as `space-y-1` with no markers and read as one run-on block at 390 px. It now uses `list-disc space-y-1.5 pl-5`, matching `EducationArticleBody`. Every test passed both before and after, because the text was present either way.
A SECOND, PRE-EXISTING DEFECT WAS FOUND AND NOT FIXED: `monthlyAllocation`'s legend has 6 entries and 4 distinct colours. See docs §6; a ratchet now guards against a new model doing the same.

ALL EIGHT new article figures were then seen in screenshots at 390 px (2026-09-17, second pass). Two further defects were found and fixed: C17's `visualReading` described THREE bars where the figure draws TWO — the budget-carried loan equals the loan used on that household, so the adapter drops the redundant bar — and C20's prose quoted only the algebraic 27,35 periods while the figure's marker says month 28. Both are prose-vs-figure disagreements that no test could see.
notObserved: 1280 as a visual observation — see `method`. DOM evidence only at that width.
Colour contrast and focus order through the eleven-field form.

OPEN, NOT A DEFECT FOUND: C21's figure carries the shared loan-chart assumption that Vietnamese home loans are promotional for 6–24 months then float. That is true of commercial loans and misleading on a social-housing article, where 5,4% is the programme rate. Left alone because that string is shared by every loan figure and is correct for the rest; it needs a per-figure override, which is its own change.
